nodes.summary: Let $a, b, c$ be integers, $n$ a natural number and $u_0, d$ rational numbers. If for every natural number $i < n$ there are rational numbers $x, y$ with $ax^2 + bxy + cy^2 = u_0 + id$, then there is a nonzero integer $k$ such that for every natural number $i < n$ there are integers $x, y$ with $ax^2 + bxy + cy^2 = k^2(u_0 + id)$.
nodes.title: Rational representations of an arithmetic progression scale to integral ones

nodes.summary: Let $a, b, c$ be integers such that the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac$ is not a perfect square. Then there are integers $u_0$ and $d \ne 0$ such that for every natural number $i < 9$ there are integers $x, y$ with $u_0 + id = ax^2 + bxy + cy^2$.
nodes.title: Binary quadratic forms with non-square discriminant represent nine-term progressions
